Run the Imagify NGG compatibility E2E spec and collect screenshots to document the results. Then update the existing QA PR comment on GitHub with the findings.

## Context

We are working on PR #1059 in wp-media/imagify-plugin (branch `fix/1020-compatibility-imagify-controls-nextgen`). This PR fixes Imagify compatibility with NextGEN Gallery v4.x.

The local WordPress environment is at http://imagify.local (or check wp-env config). NextGEN Gallery is already installed as a plugin in the workspace at:
`/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/imagify/app/public/wp-content/plugins/nextgen-gallery`

The Imagify plugin is at:
`/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/imagify/app/public/wp-content/plugins/imagify-plugin`

The E2E spec is at:
`/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/imagify/app/public/wp-content/plugins/imagify-plugin/Tests/e2e/specs/ngg-compat.spec.ts`

## What was fixed in the latest code changes (already applied)

1. `common.php`: Added `imagify_get_ngg_parent_menu_slug()` — returns `'imagely'` on NGG v4 (where the menu slug changed from `'nextgen-gallery'` to `'imagely'`).
2. `menu.php`: The Bulk Optimization submenu now registers under `imagely` on NGG v4, so it appears in the visible sidebar.
3. `ngg-compat.spec.ts`: Two new tests verify the submenu link is in `#adminmenu` and that clicking it lands on the bulk page.

## Your tasks

### 1. Ensure NGG is activated

Check if NextGEN Gallery is active. If not, activate it using WP-CLI. The WordPress install is at:
`/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/imagify/app/public`

Use wp-cli like: `wp --path="/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/imagify/app/public" plugin activate nextgen-gallery`

### 2. Run the E2E tests

Find and run the ngg-compat spec. The project likely has a playwright config. Try:
```
cd /Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/imagify/app/public/wp-content/plugins/imagify-plugin
IMAGIFY_NGG_INSTALLED=1 npx playwright test Tests/e2e/specs/ngg-compat.spec.ts --headed=false 2>&1
```

If that fails, look at the playwright.config.ts to find the right command and base URL.

### 3. Take screenshots of key UI states using Playwright

Use Playwright (mcp__playwright tools) to:
a. Navigate to the NGG v4 gallery page (`/wp-admin/admin.php?page=imagely`) — take a screenshot showing the sidebar with the "Bulk Optimization" submenu item under the Imagely menu.
b. Click the "Bulk Optimization" link and take a screenshot of the resulting page.
c. Navigate to the new NGG v4 gallery image list page and take a screenshot of the three-dot context menu to show there is NO Imagify option (documenting the per-image limitation).

The admin URL is likely http://imagify.local/wp-admin/. WordPress admin credentials: check for a local config or try admin/password or admin/admin.

### 4. Report your findings

Report back with:
- Which tests passed/failed
- Screenshot file paths (saved to `/Users/gaelrobin/Local Sites/imagify/app/public/wp-content/plugins/imagify-plugin/.github/qa-screenshots/` or wherever is appropriate)
- The full markdown body for a PR comment update (see format below)

### 5. Update the existing PR comment

The existing QA comment on PR #1059 has comment ID `4493431550` (author: Miraeld).

Update it using:
```
gh api repos/wp-media/imagify-plugin/issues/comments/4493431550 \
  --method PATCH \
  --field body="<updated comment body>"
```

The updated comment body should:
- Keep the existing test report structure (acceptance criteria table, etc.)
- Add a new section for the bulk submenu fix with test results and screenshots
- Add a section explicitly documenting the per-image optimization limitation with the technical reason (React SPA with no PHP extension hooks — see explanation below)
- Note which tests are new vs previously covered

## Per-image limitation explanation (include this in the comment)

The per-image Imagify column that existed in NGG v3 relied on PHP filters (`ngg_manage_images_number_of_columns`, `ngg_manage_images_column_{N}_header/content`) on the legacy `nggallery-manage-gallery` page. NGG v4 replaced that page with a React SPA under `admin.php?page=imagely`. The React bundle's image context menu is hardcoded — there are no PHP hooks for third-party plugins to inject actions. The only PHP filter (`ngg_imagely_app_data`) passes config to JS but the app only reads `adminURL` and `assetsURL`. No `wp.hooks`/`applyFilters` API is used in the bundle either. Therefore per-image optimization cannot be restored without NGG exposing an extension point.

## Important notes

- If the WP environment is not running (wp-env), try to start it or use the local site directly.
- If Playwright can't connect, check the baseURL in playwright config and try with `--base-url http://imagify.local`.
- Do NOT modify any source PHP/TS files — only run tests and post the GitHub comment.
- If you cannot run tests, at minimum use Playwright MCP to navigate the admin and take screenshots manually.

# Description

Fixes #1020

Restores Imagify optimization controls (bulk menu item + per-image column) inside the NextGEN Gallery admin interface for users running NextGEN Gallery v4.x+.

After NextGEN Gallery v4.0.0 (released December 2025), the plugin underwent a complete UI/UX revamp. As part of this, the POPE mixin framework (`Mixin` class and `C_Gallery_Storage`) is no longer eagerly initialized at plugin-load time. The Imagify bootstrap guard `class_exists('Mixin')` therefore evaluated to `false`, silently preventing the entire NGG compatibility layer from loading. As a result, neither the **Bulk Optimization** submenu nor the **per-image optimization column** appeared in the NextGEN Gallery admin.

This fix removes the stale `Mixin` class gate from the bootstrap condition and wraps the internal `C_Gallery_Storage::add_mixin()` call with defensive class-existence checks, so it no-ops gracefully on NGG v4.x while remaining fully backwards-compatible with NGG v3.x.

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue).
- [ ] Enhancement (non-breaking change which improves an existing functionality).
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as before).
- [ ] Sub-task of #1020

- [ ] Release

## Detailed scenario

| Bulk Optimization submenu in NGG v4.x menu | Analysis: traced bootstrap gate → admin menu hook | ✅ PASS |
| No PHP fatal error on NGG v4.x | Analysis: inspected `add_mixin()` call path | ✅ PASS |
| No regression on NGG v3.x | Analysis: inspected v3.x code path | ✅ PASS |

Full QA report: https://github.com/wp-media/imagify-plugin/pull/1059#issuecomment-4493431550

### How to test

**Pre-conditions:**
- WordPress installation with Imagify active.
- NextGEN Gallery v4.x installed and active (latest: v4.2.1).
- At least one gallery with images created.

**Test 1 — Bulk Optimization menu:**
1. Go to the NextGEN Gallery admin menu (left sidebar → "Gallery").
2. Verify that a "Bulk Optimization" submenu item appears under the Gallery menu.
3. Click it and confirm the Imagify bulk optimization page loads correctly.

**Test 2 — Per-image optimization column (NGG v4.x React UI):**
- Note: In NGG v4.x, gallery management uses a React-based SPA. The legacy PHP column hooks (`ngg_manage_images_number_of_columns`) no longer fire in this view. The individual image optimization column is a known NGG v4.x limitation that requires NGG to expose React extension points for third-party integrations. This is tracked as a follow-up.
- With NGG v3.x (pre-v4.0), verify that the "Imagify" column still appears in Manage Galleries → image list.

**Test 3 — No fatal errors on NGG v4.x:**
1. Activate both plugins.
2. Navigate any admin page.
3. Confirm no PHP fatal errors or critical notices related to `Mixin` or `C_Gallery_Storage`.

**Test 4 — Regression on NGG v3.x:**
1. Roll back NGG to v3.59.12.
2. Confirm the Bulk Optimization menu item appears.
3. Confirm the per-image Imagify column appears in gallery management.
4. Confirm no errors in the PHP error log.
